J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges "Cij = delta(Si) is a bond." First-choice line 35 reads "Let Cij != empty for some pair (i, j). We prove that Cij = delta(Si) is a bond." Taken as written the line asserts the identification C_ij = delta(S_i) (and that this set is a bond). The assumptions in force are those of Steps 1-2: G undirected, V = S disjoint union T with both non-empty (Definition 1, lines 4-7), S_1..S_p the components of G[S] and T_1..T_q the components of G[T] (lines 18-21), C_ij the edges of C from S_i to T_j (line 24), and C_ij non-empty (line 35 itself). Nothing there forces q = 1, so the asserted equality is a general claim.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: A fully explicit graph with the two sets computed: "Take G with S = {a,b} (edge ab, so G[S] has one component S1), T = {c,d,e} where {c,d} is an edge and e is isolated (giving T components T1={c,d} and T2={e}), and edges a-c and a-e. Then C11 = {a-c} but delta(S1) = {a-c, a-e}, so C11 != delta(S1)." Vertices, edges, the partition, both component decompositions and both sets are given.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Exact finite computation of the supplied witness, script kept. With V = {a,b,c,d,e} and E = {ab, cd, ac, ae}, S = {a,b} and T = {c,d,e} is a legitimate cut partition (both parts non-empty); G[S] has the single component S_1 = {a,b} and G[T] has the two components T_1 = {c,d} and T_2 = {e}, exactly as the response says. Then C = delta(S) = {ac, ae}, C_11 = {ac} (non-empty, so the hypothesis of line 35 holds) and C_12 = {ae}, while delta(S_1) = {ac, ae}. So C_11 is a strict subset of delta(S_1) and the equality asserted at line 35 is false on an instance meeting every assumption in force there; the refutation is of the line as written. I also recorded that in this same witness C_11 = {ac} is nevertheless a bond (deleting it raises the component count from 1 to 2 and no proper subset is a cut), so what the witness refutes is the identification C_ij = delta(S_i), not the claim that C_ij is a bond.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The response's stated consequence is narrow and accurate: "So delta(Si) = union over j of Cij. Indeed ... So claiming Cij = delta(Si) is false unless q=1", and it locates that at line 35. It explicitly declines to attack the theorem, having worked through the argument and concluded "Thus theorem might be true" and that the decomposition into the C_ij is genuinely disjoint. No overreach.

notes: For the adjudicator: what the response refutes is the equality inside line 35, not the line's substantive claim (that each non-empty C_ij is a bond), which holds in the witness and, as the response itself reasons, appears to hold in general. So this is a real but local defect -- the proof mislabels C_ij as delta(S_i), which is correct only when q = 1 -- and a reader who requires the located assertion to be load-bearing for the argument's conclusion may weigh it differently. Under the 'false as written' framing the line does assert a false equality and the witness is exact. Note too that the source's own line 49 partially corrects itself ("More precisely, Cij is a subset of delta(Tj)"), which supports reading line 35's equality as an assertion the author later walks back rather than a slip of notation.
